Floss
FLAWSS
noun / verb (Gen Alpha slang)
A dance in which the arms swing side to side in front of and behind the body while the hips swing the other way, like pulling dental floss. Popularized by Russell Horning, "the Backpack Kid," in a 2016 Instagram video and made famous when he danced it beside Katy Perry on Saturday Night Live in May 2017; Fortnite made it an emote in 2018 and the floss became the worldwide schoolyard dance of that year (some schools banned it in class). Horning sued Epic Games in December 2018 and later dropped the suit. Older senses of floss: silk fibers, and (1990s hip-hop) to show off.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The floss is the arm-swinging dance that every Gen Alpha child of 2018 could do, and many still do — at recess, at weddings, in the cereal aisle. It is pure silly motion. The Christian observation: like most children’s dances, it is one of the small joys, and joy is God’s idea. "Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing" (Psa 30:11), and a whole people sang that God would "joy over thee with singing" (Zep 3:17). Children who move their bodies in delight are doing something their Creator made them to do. There is one older slang sense a parent should know: in 1990s hip-hop, to floss meant to show off wealth — flashy jewelry, cars — and Scripture has a word for that, too: "Let not the rich man glory in his riches: but let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me" (Jer 9:23-24). The Gen Alpha floss is the dance, not the boast. A father can tell a five-year-old: "Show me your floss! God made your arms and your legs and your happy heart — you can dance for Him." The father who learns the floss badly is giving his daughter a memory and a laugh, which are gifts too.

Webster 1828 Definition

The arm-swinging dance of the Backpack Kid (2016; SNL 2017; Fortnite 2018) — harmless joy in motion; its older hip-hop sense, to show off wealth, is the one Jeremiah rebukes.

FLOSS, n. / v. (dance, 2016–present; Gen Alpha usage) A dance of swinging arms and counter-swinging hips; to do the dance. "She can floss so fast."

1990s hip-hop sense: to floss, to flaunt wealth (still heard in older rap).

Original sense: silk fibers; dental floss, the thread for cleaning teeth.

Decode for parents: the dance is harmless; the show-off sense is the one worth a talk.

Webster 1828, the root — FLOSS, n. A downy or silky substance in the husks of certain plants.

Key Scripture

Psa 30:11 — "Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness;"

Zep 3:17 — "The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing."

Jer 9:23 — "Thus saith the LORD, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches:"

Jer 9:24 — "But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD."

Modern Corruption

The floss dance is harmless joy; the older slang sense — to floss, to flaunt wealth — is the boast of the rich man Jeremiah forbids.

expand to see more

Children’s dance crazes come and go, and the floss is among the most innocent: no lyrics, no gesture beyond silliness. The only real ground for caution is the word’s other life in hip-hop, where flossing meant displaying jewelry and money — the glory in riches that Scripture names as vain.

Enjoy the dance, and teach the distinction. We dance because we are glad, not to show what we own. If the child ever hears "flossin’" in a song about money, tell her Jeremiah’s word: glory in knowing God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old French flosche (down, nap) → English floss (silk fiber, dental floss) → 1990s hip-hop floss (to show off) → the Backpack Kid’s dance (2016–18).
